input.question: How is Titan able to have an atmosphere pressure similar to Earth when it's gravity is so much lower than Earth's?
input.ground_truth: Cold makes sticky. Titan can hang on to so much atmosphere even though it’s gravity is much weaker, because the cold temperature means the collisions of gas particles are less energetic. Thus less likely to bounce hard enough that Titans gravity can’t recollect them.

Titan is a smaller and lighter planet than Earth, so it doesn't pull as hard on things. That means if you jump on Titan, you'd float higher and things wouldn't fall as fast as on Earth.

Now, the air (or atmosphere) around a planet is like a big blanket that hugs it. Earth has a strong gravity, so its blanket stays tight and squished down. That's why Earth's air is heavy and pushes hard on us (that's called high pressure).

Titan has weaker gravity, so its blanket isn't squished as much. But here's the cool part: Titan's air is made mostly of a gas called nitrogen, and it has a lot of this gas. Even though the gravity is weaker, there's so much gas that it still pushes down on the surface with about the same pressure as Earth's air does!

So, even though Titan is lighter and its gravity is weaker, it has enough air to make the pressure at the surface about the same as on Earth. It's like having a big, thick blanket instead of a small, heavy one.
